newsitem.title: USA: Hancock consents to repayment, penalties.
newsitem.headline: Hancock consents to repayment, penalties.

text.p: Boston-based John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co agreed to repay $650,000 to its pension plan and pay the federal government $130,000 in civil penalties, the U.S. Labor Department said on Tuesday.

Under an agreement filed in Boston's U.S. District Court, Hancock neither admitted nor denied the charges in a civil suit brought by the Labor Department that it had used its own subsidiary, Independent Investment Associates, to manage the fund.

In a March lawsuit, the Labor Department alleged Hancock retained the subsidiary to manage a portion of the plan's assets in March 1986 and allowed the plan to pay more than $615,000 in fees to that subsidiary. Federal pension law prohibits paying a subsidiary for managing plan funds except as a reimbursement of actual expenses.
The pension plan covered 9,953 participants and had more than $500 million in assets in 1993, according to the Labor Department.
John Hancock spokesmen were not available for comment.
